req.title: Redirect-to supports custom status codes
req.statement: The system shall honour the 'status_code' query parameter on /redirect-to for values 301, 302, 303, 307, and 308.

doc.reasoning: The redirect_to() handler reads 'status_code' from query args, validates it is in [300,400), and sets response.status_code accordingly. To kill mutations we must: (1) assert exact status codes for each valid value (301,302,303,307,308); (2) test the boundary at 300 (inclusive lower bound) and 399 (inclusive upper bound); (3) test 299 and 400 which must NOT be honoured (boundary ±1 outside range); (4) test missing status_code falls back to 302; (5) test the Location header is set to the exact URL supplied. Each test uses Flask test_client with follow_redirects=False to capture the raw redirect response.

tests.name: test_redirect_to_status_301
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_status_301():
    r = client.get('/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=301', follow_redirects=False)
    assert r.status_code == 301
    assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_status_301()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact
actions: Iterate over [301,302,303,307,308] and GET /redirect-to with each status_code
expected: Each response status code matches the requested code exactly
trace: R-HTTPBIN-025: all five required codes must be honoured; catches constant-mutation on any one code
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact():
    for code in [301, 302, 303, 307, 308]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=' + str(code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == code, f'Expected {code}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.headers['Location'] == 'http://example.com'

test_redirect_to_all_valid_codes_exact()

tests.name: test_redirect_to_invalid_non_3xx_codes_ignored
actions: Iterate over [200,201,404,500] and GET /redirect-to with each status_code
expected: Each response status code is exactly 302 (default), not the supplied non-3xx code
trace: R-HTTPBIN-025: non-3xx status_code values must be ignored; catches missing range check mutations
tests.executable:
from httpbin.core import app
client = app.test_client()

def test_redirect_to_invalid_non_3xx_codes_ignored():
    for bad_code in [200, 201, 404, 500]:
        r = client.get(
            '/redirect-to?url=http://example.com&status_code=' + str(bad_code),
            follow_redirects=False
        )
        assert r.status_code == 302, f'Expected 302 for bad code {bad_code}, got {r.status_code}'
        assert r.status_code != bad_code

test_redirect_to_invalid_non_3xx_codes_ignored()
